patient_actor_hidden.History: The patient presents with a year-long history of severe vulvar itching and pain during sexual intercourse that has gradually worsened. She has tried over-the-counter lubricants without significant relief. Menopause occurred 8 years ago. Her medical history is significant for diet-controlled type 2 diabetes mellitus and hypertension treated with hydrochlorothiazide.
patient_actor_hidden.Past_Medical_History: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (diet-controlled), hypertension (treated with hydrochlorothiazide), menopause at 52 years of age.
patient_actor_hidden.Social_History: Married, sexually active with her husband until recently due to severe pain. Non-smoker, drinks alcohol socially.
patient_actor_hidden.Review_of_Systems: Denies urinary incontinence, postcoital bleeding, or recent changes in skin elsewhere on the body.

objective_for_doctor: Evaluate and manage a patient presenting with vulvar itching and discomfort.

turns.doctor_opening: Hello, what brings you in today? Could you tell me about yourself and what's been going on?
turns.patient_opening: “Doctor, I’m a 60-year-old woman, and over the past year I’ve had severe itching and burning in my vulvar area, which has gradually worsened. Sex has become extremely painful for me, and the over-the-counter lubricants haven’t helped much.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any swelling in your joints?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed any swelling or pain in my joints. It’s mostly focused on the vulvar itching and burning, and the discomfort becomes especially intense during intercourse.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any bumps, sores, or unusual spots on your scalp?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed any bumps, sores, or unusual spots on my scalp. The problem has been mainly in the vulvar area—intense itching and burning, and it gets much worse during intercourse.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you been experiencing any itching or a feeling of itchiness anywhere on your body?
turns.patient_answer: “No, it’s mainly in my vulvar area—there isn’t itching elsewhere on my body. Occasionally it feels more intense after sex, but otherwise it’s pretty localized to the vulva.”

turns.doctor_question: Do you have any trouble lifting your arms above your head?
turns.patient_answer: “Doctor, I don’t have trouble lifting my arms above my head—my main problem is the localized severe vulvar itching and burning, which is especially intense during intercourse.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any loss of vision that isn’t accompanied by pain?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t had any vision loss, and there isn’t any eye pain either. My symptoms are still mainly severe vulvar itching and burning that’s especially intense during intercourse.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you had a fever that’s felt extremely hot—like a temperature above 104 °F (40 °C) that’s made you feel dizzy or very uncomfortable?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t had any fever or felt extremely hot like that, and I don’t have dizziness from a high temperature. It’s really just the severe vulvar itching and burning—especially during intercourse—that’s been worsening over the past year.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you been feeling unusually stressed or overwhelmed lately?
turns.patient_answer: “Doctor, I wouldn’t say I’ve been unusually stressed or overwhelmed, since it’s mostly the persistent, localized vulvar itching and burning that’s been getting worse—particularly during intercourse.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you experienced any burning or discomfort when you urinate?
turns.patient_answer: “Doctor, I don’t really have burning or discomfort when I urinate—most of the burning and pain is in the vulvar area, and it becomes especially intense during intercourse.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you been feeling chills lately?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t had chills. It’s been mainly the severe localized vulvar itching and burning that’s been steadily worsening, especially during intercourse.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any lumps or masses in your breasts that feel fixed or don’t move?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed any lumps or fixed masses in my breasts. My main issue is still the severe vulvar itching and burning, especially during intercourse.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you been feeling any pain or discomfort on the side of your back or abdomen, between your ribs and hips?
turns.patient_answer: “Doctor, I haven’t had pain or discomfort in my back or abdomen between my ribs and hips. It’s been almost entirely localized to my vulvar area, with the itching and burning especially intense during intercourse.”

turns.doctor_question: Do you feel pain in your calf when you walk, and does it go away when you stop and rest?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed any calf pain when I walk or that goes away with rest—I don’t think this is affecting my legs. My symptoms are still mainly severe vulvar itching and burning, and it gets much worse during intercourse.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed that your urine looks darker than usual?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed my urine looking darker than usual. My main issue remains the severe vulvar itching and burning, which gets especially intense during intercourse.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any difficulty moving your arm up or across your body?
turns.patient_answer: “No, doctor—I don’t have any trouble moving my arms up or across my body. My symptoms are still mainly severe, localized vulvar itching and burning that gets much worse during intercourse.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed that your joints feel sore or stiff after doing the same activity repeatedly, like after a long day of typing, lifting, or other repetitive motions?
turns.patient_answer: “Doctor, I haven’t noticed any joint soreness or stiffness after repetitive activities—my discomfort is really only the severe localized vulvar itching and burning, and it becomes much worse during intercourse.”
